question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[Y\sqrt{X}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2{y}^{3}},\, & 0\le x\le 4,\,1\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=y\sqrt{x}.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonzero only in the rectangular region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,1\le y\le 2\}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\sqrt{X}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}y\sqrt{x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\sqrt{x}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4}y\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{x}}{2{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{2{y}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{2{y}^{2}}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{4}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4[-\frac{1}{y}]_{1}^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
